Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

###

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

###

Why Firmus?

As an NVIDIA Cloud and Engineering partner in Asia Pacific, you will gain skills, experience, and exposure across the AI industry and be part of shaping what this industry looks like for decades to come.

We are founder-led, not a big corporate. Decisions happen fast, our leaders are accessible, and there's minimum bureaucracy between you and the work. Ownership comes early. Whatever your role, you will have a direct line to outcomes, helping shape how the business grows as we scale nationally across a long-term, large-scale roadmap.

Work alongside founders and experts in AI infrastructure, energy systems and next-generation compute.

What we build here has impact beyond the business. Our AI Factories are designed to operate as assets to the energy grid to actively strengthen the communities and regions they operate in rather than drawing from them.

Considering applying? You don't need a perfect background to join our team. If you're driven and curious, there's a path for you. We back our people to grow into new domains and take on challenges beyond their previous experience.

Role Summary

Reporting to the General Manager, Investor Relations, the Team Coordinator, Investor Relations provides the coordination and operating support that keeps the IR program moving: the calendar, meetings, materials, CRM, register, disclosure workflow, adviser coordination and interfaces with Legal, Finance, Communications and Company Secretary.

This is a meaningful coordination role, not a general administration role. It is suited to someone with 5+ years of experience who is organised, discreet, curious and able to bring structure to complex work while continuing to develop judgement in a listed-company environment.

The role works closely with the Senior Manager and GM, IR, providing the cadence, workflow and information discipline that allow investor engagement, reporting and disclosure processes to run well.

Key Responsibilities

IR Calendar, Meetings and Roadshow Logistics

  • Coordinate the IR calendar, including results, trading updates, AGMs, investor days, roadshows, conferences and one-on-one meetings.

Materials, Disclosure Workflow and Document Control

  • Coordinate production, version control and sign-off tracking for investor materials, ASX announcements, presentations, annual reporting content and shareholder communications.
  • Support the disclosure workflow in partnership with Legal and Company Secretariat, including trafficking drafts, tracking comments, managing sign-off checklists and coordinating ASX release logistics.
  • Coordinate investor website updates, webcast logistics, presentation uploads and digital investor materials with Communications, Legal, IT and external providers.

Investor CRM, Register and Data

  • Coordinate the day-to-day operation of the investor CRM, including logging interactions, maintaining contact records, and running reports for management and the Board.
  • Coordinate shareholder register monitoring, share registry requests, targeting lists, proxy adviser tracking and analyst coverage records.

Stakeholder Coordination and Team Support

  • Coordinate with capital markets advisers, legal counsel, PR advisers, share registry and other external providers on process, timelines and deliverables.

**

Skills & Experience

Essential

  • 5+ years of experience in coordination, program management, executive support, corporate affairs, capital markets operations or corporate access, ideally in a listed-company, transaction, professional services or investment banking environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder processes involving senior executives, external advisers, legal counsel, governance stakeholders or investors.
  • Strong written communication, attention to detail and document discipline, including the ability to produce executive-ready materials and maintain clear version control.
  • Strong organisational skills across calendar management, travel, events, workflow tracking, meeting preparation and follow-up.
  • Familiarity with IR, governance or capital markets operating tools and processes, including Microsoft 365, IR CRM tools, share registry platforms, market data services, virtual data rooms or equivalent systems.
  • High discretion, sound judgement and experience handling confidential or market-sensitive information appropriately.
  • Curiosity, structured problem-solving and comfort working through unfamiliar tasks where there is no obvious template.
  • Experience supporting Board, Company Secretary, governance, investor meeting, roadshow, event or cross-time-zone coordination processes.

Desirable

  • Exposure to technology, infrastructure, energy, AI, data centres or other complex project-based sectors.

What we are looking for

We are looking for someone who brings high standards, sound judgement and ownership to a coordination role at the centre of a busy IR function. The role provides operating leverage to the GM, IR and Senior Manager, IR with close exposure to how investor messaging, disclosure processes and market engagement come together.

The right person communicates clearly, learns quickly, improves process, and brings structure to complex work. You are proactive, organised and reliable, with the judgement to know when to move forward and when to pause, check and escalate.

###

Location & Reporting

  • Location: Sydney, NSW, Australia
  • Reports to: General Manager, Investor Relations

Employment Basis

Permanent full-time

Diversity

At Firmus, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are passionate about creating a more sustainable future through innovative engineering solutions.

Join us in our mission to revolutionise the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

job.title: Strategic Writer
job.description:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

Role Summary

Firmus builds and operates AI factories - the industrial plants of the intelligence age. We design, manufacture, construct, own and operate the full stack: from the grid connection and energy systems, through our own cooling and power infrastructure, to the GPU clusters and the software that runs them. Energy in, tokens out.

We are not a data centre company. We are a process industry, converting renewable energy and GPU supply into AI compute at a cost of production we believe no operator starting today can match. Our facilities are engineered from the GPU outward, manufactured in our own supply chain, and operated against contracts with some of the world's largest and most progressive technology companies operating at the frontier of AI development.

The scale of what we are building means our impact is felt well beyond technology: in national energy markets, where our demand unlocks stranded renewable generation; in regional economies, where gigawatt-scale industrial investment lands; and in national capability, where sovereign AI infrastructure is becoming a strategic asset. Writing about Firmus means writing about all of it - compute, energy, capital, and policy - with numbers that hold up.

Firmus runs on narrative as much as it runs on engineering. The same story - what we build, how it performs, what it costs, why it matters - has to hold together across our website, investor presentations, customer materials, government submissions, and thought leadership, told at different depths for different audiences but never contradicting itself.

The Strategic Writer owns that coherence. You are the person who can sit with an engineer in the morning and understand why our cooling architecture impacts the efficiency of AI Token production, then explain it that afternoon in a response to the media, a minister, communities where we have sites, or the front page of our website - accurately, and in their language. You write across the full surface of the business and our audiences, and you are the keeper of how Firmus sounds.

This is not a documentation role. You will describe our products technically and credibly, but you will not be writing API references, operations manuals, or engineering specifications. You will join the company with a well-established narrative and story, and pick up the pen as a full time owner of the cohesiveness of this story, and applying it consistently as it develops.

Key Responsibilities

Narrative Ownership

  • Help to hold the master narrative across the business - one coherent story from website to corporate - and keep every piece of external writing consistent with it.
  • Maintain and evolve the Firmus tone of voice: confident, precise, commercially realistic.
  • Act as the writing standard-setter for external materials produced across teams.

Core Communication Assets

  • Write and maintain the company's primary expressions of itself: website copy, corporate presentations, media statements, community information, company profiles, capability statements.
  • Develop presentation content with leadership, customers, partners, and conferences.
  • Ensure flagship materials stay current as the business scales - capacity, projects, partnerships, milestones, key metrics and claims
  • Ensure consistency in application of design of written materials across the business

Technical Product Writing

  • Describe Firmus's technology and platforms - cooling architecture, power systems, factory operations software, energy integration - with genuine technical fluency, at the depth each audience needs.
  • Describe Firmus’s AI Cloud product features and details across a number of mediums
  • Work directly with engineering and infrastructure teams so every technical claim is accurate, measurable, and defensible.
  • Translate engineering decisions into commercial meaning: why a design choice shows up in cost, performance, or reliability.

Thought Leadership

  • Identify where Firmus has earned the right to a public point of view, and build the written case for it.
  • Lead Firmus' thought leadership strategy in line with the overarching corporate and product communications strategy
  • Produce articles, papers, and explainers on the technical and economic substance of AI infrastructure — energy demand, cooling, compute economics, grid integration — under company and executive bylines.

Policy and Government-Facing Content

  • Draft briefing papers, submissions, and explanatory material for government stakeholders on AI infrastructure, energy demand, and national capability.
  • Bridge technical reality and policy expectations on AI, energy use, sustainability, and economic impact.

Accuracy and Credibility

  • Maintain factual accuracy, numerical integrity, and traceability in everything published.
  • Validate metrics, assumptions, and claims with internal teams as required before anything is published externally
  • Be deliberate about disclosure. What is said, to whom, and what is not.

Skills & Experience

  • Experience writing about AI infrastructure, data centres, energy systems, or large-scale technical platforms.
  • Strong capability in working with numbers: capacity, performance, cost, efficiency, and growth metrics.
  • Demonstrated experience producing commercially oriented technical or policy content.
  • Ability to engage deeply with technical and commercial stakeholders and extract what materially matters.
  • Comfort operating in environments where accuracy and credibility directly affect commercial and policy outcomes.
  • Write with an understanding of cost, scale, and operational constraints.
  • Test claims against data, not aspiration.
  • Understand that in AI and compute infrastructure, credibility is a commercial asset.
  • You are deliberate about what is said, and what is not.

Key Competencies

  • Strong communication (technical + non-technical audiences)
  • Strong ability to understand diverse angles of complicated issues, and tell a consistent narrative
  • Attention to detail, consistency in approach to writing, formatting and presentation
  • Managing multiple deadlines and competing priorities
  • Demonstrated leadership & ownership
  • Problem-solving under ambiguity

Location & Reporting

  • The right candidate can be based in Sydney or Melbourne, Australia, or in Singapore.
  • Reports directly to GM Corporate Communications, works alongside GM Product & Brand Communications and Co-CEO

Employment Basis

Full-time

Diversity

At Firmus, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are passionate about creating a more sustainable future through innovative engineering solutions.

Join us in our mission to revolutionise the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

ROLE SUMMARY

Firmus Technologies is seeking a skilled Site Reliability Engineer to join our Operations team, supporting the daily operations and maintenance of our AI-accelerated high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. This role will work closely with Field Service Engineers, HPC and Network Engineering teams, and assist the Global Operations Centre (GOC). This is a unique opportunity to contribute directly to the stability and growth of cutting-edge AI infrastructure.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support in the deployment, configuration, and maintenance of various high-end GPU servers, storage servers, networking equipment and software components in highly secure environments.
  • Perform hardware diagnostics, systems functionality and firmware updates as required.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to assist in tailored customer environments deployment (eg: bare-metal systems, HPC Clusters, Kubernetes, Slurm etc).
  • Serve as first line of engineering support for onsite operational issues, including troubleshooting hardware, network and software problems, and firmware compliance.
  • Troubleshoot incidents, escalate critical issues and provide feedback to appropriate teams for improvements.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure 24/7 availability and responsiveness to critical issues.
  • Provide technical support to the GOC Support Specialist team in troubleshooting compute infrastructure related problems.
  • Document incident details, resolutions, and lessons learned to enhance future problem-solving.
  • Maintain clear, accurate, and up-to-date documentation to promote effective knowledge sharing across the team.
  • Communicate effectively with GOC, HPC Engineers, internal teams, stakeholders, and end-users to ensure alignment on issue resolution.
  • Take part in team meetings and knowledge-sharing sessions to foster collaboration and continuous learning.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
  • 5+ years of experience in field service technical areas.
  • Strong understanding of server hardware technology, firmware lifecycle, Linux environments and troubleshooting hardware problems, with adherence to physical and system-level security standards.
  • Experience with scripting languages (eg: Bash, Python)
  • Familiarity with using configuration management, CICD tools, workload manager and cluster softwares (eg: Slurm, Kubernetes, Nvidia BCM) and Observability tools (eg: Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, etc)
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

Location

This role is based in Launceston, Tasmania, Australia.

Employment Basis

Full-time

job.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
job.description:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

Role Summary

We are seeking a versatile Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the end-to-end delivery of complex, large-scale technical programs at Firmus. Depending on the assignment, you may be externally facing – managing delivery with our key customers, including major hyper-scalers and frontier model builders – or internally facing, driving the strategic infrastructure and platform programs that power Firmus AI Cloud. In both cases, you will act as the bridge between engineering, operations, and business teams to ensure initiatives land with minimal disruption and maximum value.

As the owner of program delivery, you will translate ambiguity into structured, phased plans, manage complex technical dependencies across stakeholders, and keep everyone aligned from working teams through to executive leadership. You will drive implementation, ensure milestones and adoption targets are met, establish feedback loops, and make the technical trade-off decisions that balance delivery velocity with customer and business impact—whether the “customer” sits outside the company or within it.

Key Responsibilities

You’ll own the delivery of your programs end to end – turning ambiguous goals into structured, phased plans with clear scope, timelines, and milestones, and running the operating rhythm of daily or weekly syncs, executive status meetings, and stakeholder communications that keep everyone aligned on readiness, roadmaps, and impact. Throughout, you’ll make the technical trade-off decisions that balance internal velocity against customer and business impact.

Depending on the assignment, that delivery is either externally facing—acting as the trusted point of contact for major hyper-scalers and frontier model builders, owning customer communications and advisories, and driving adoption milestones and feedback loops—or internally facing, leading the cross-team platform and infrastructure programs that power Firmus AI Cloud and aligning internal sponsors and engineering leaders on roadmaps and delivery. Either way, you’ll apply the same rigour and stakeholder discipline.

Across both, you’ll bring enough command of our systems—AI Factory architecture, GPU performance and benchmarking, and infrastructure constraints—to answer questions directly and validate impact assessments rather than just relaying between teams. You’ll orchestrate delivery across engineering, operations, and customer-facing functions, and run a regular leadership cadence to manage escalations and hold communication timelines.

Skills & Experience

You’ll bring at least 10 years in Technical Program or Project Management, including 4+ years leading large-scale transformation programs, whether that’s with direct external customer exposure or delivering internal enterprise programs. Just as important is technical fluency across the AI/ML stack: a robust understanding of AI hardware, large-scale networks, and cloud architectures, grounded in practical experience building, scaling, and operating high-density infrastructure and systems.

Communication is central to this role. You can draft a customer-facing advisory that is clear, empathetic, and technically accurate – not a cut-and-paste from an LLM – and you use a range of tools (like Jira) day to day to build the artifacts and plans that organize, communicate, and drive customer and program success. You pair this with strong stakeholder management across Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and internal engineering leaders, and you’re comfortable in high-ambiguity environments where program structures often need to be created rather than simply followed.

Ideally, you bring a proven track record delivering programs such as enterprise feature rollouts with customer-specific configurations, cloud migrations for enterprise customers, large-scale GPU infrastructure or data-centre buildouts, and internal platform migrations or cross-team infrastructure rollouts.

Location & Reporting

  • Based in Sydney, Australia
  • Reports directly to CTO in the interim

job.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
job.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

**

Firmus Technologies is seeking an experienced Senior Mechanical Engineer in the Data Centre Infrastructure domain specifically in the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) area to join our Engineering and Technology team. The successful candidate will be involved end-to-end in the design, engineering, commissioning and operational support of Firmus’ state-of-the-art sustainable AI Factory developments.

This role is based in Singapore, but travel is expected (10-30% time), primarily during the delivery phases of projects.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop design and key documentation from concept to commissioning.
  • Assist in technical qualification, onboarding and management of third-party consultants and contractors.
  • Carry out engineering design and calculations to provide system design for contractors.
  • Provide final equipment selections including required capacities and efficiencies for procurement and construction.
  • Review consultant designs.
  • Review contractor mechanical workshop drawings and equipment selections.
  • Assist in the creation of Operation and Maintenance manuals that shall include all maintenance requirements of systems and equipment.
  • Carry out site inspections to ensure the installation is in-line with the relevant documentation and specifications.
  • Participate in the commissioning of mechanical systems and ensure equipment and plant is operating at optimum performance.
  • Develop technical engineering standards.
  • Engage in R&D initiatives and design optimisation.
  • Mentor junior engineers and assist with their technical development

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering.
  • 8+ years of experience with a minimum of 5 years of Data Centre MEP experience.
  • Strong working knowledge of heat transfer and fluid dynamics fundamentals including the application of appropriate international design standards (e.g. ASHRAE)
  • Familiarity with the Asia Pacific region and the application of local DC standards and norms is advantageous.
  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills with an innate ability to work with ambiguous problems and develop effective and innovative technical solutions.
  • Detail-oriented approach to work to ensure accuracy in design and testing and strong clear documentation.
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. The ability to articulate ideas and convey technical information to non-technical stakeholders is a must.
  • Demonstrated experience of working in a cross-functional multi-cultural teams.
  • Excellent collaboration, organisation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Strong willingness to learn and proactively contribute to team and organisational goals.
  • Flexibility to adapt to evolving project requirements and priorities with an eagerness to take on new responsibilities and learn on the job.

Considering applying? You don't need a perfect background to join our team. If you're driven and curious, there's a path for you. We back our people to grow into new domains and take on challenges beyond their previous experience.

Role Summary

The Senior Treasury Specialist will support Firmus’ treasury operations across debt facilities, hedging, cash management, bank guarantees, intercompany funding, reporting, controls, and treasury systems implementation.

This role is responsible for helping build scalable treasury processes as Firmus grows, ensuring treasury activity is accurately captured, controlled, reported, and aligned with financing, accounting, compliance, and operational requirements.

  • Debt facility administration, including ongoing management of monthly compliance processes for GPU backed asset financings.
  • FX and interest rate hedging, including confirmation processes, FX and interest rate settlements, hedge accounting support, valuations, and effectiveness testing inputs.
  • Cash management and investments, including short-term liquidity planning, consolidated cash reporting, investments and counterparty exposure monitoring.
  • Treasury systems and automation, including implementation of a treasury management system, automated bank feeds, straight-through processing, and improved treasury controls.

You will work closely with Finance, Legal, Company Secretariat, Operations, and external banking partners to ensure treasury processes are disciplined, accurate, timely, and fit for a fast-growing AI infrastructure business.

The role is hands-on and operationally focused, requiring strong attention to detail, control discipline, financial systems capability, and the ability to manage multiple treasury work streams across debt, hedging, cash, reporting, and intercompany activity.

This position is ideal for someone who enjoys building robust treasury operations in a high-growth environment and can combine technical treasury knowledge with practical process execution.

Key Responsibilities

Debt Facilities

  • Maintain accurate records of debt facilities, including key terms, rate sets, interest accruals, fee amortisation, ticking fees, and related accounting inputs.
  • Prepare and coordinate monthly compliance processes, covenant reporting, certificates, lender reporting, and ongoing covenant model updates.
  • Coordinate treasury payments for based on debt waterfalls, and manage fees, interest, transfers to and from liquidity accounts, and other facility-related cash movements.

Cash Management & Investments

  • Prepare consolidated cash balance reporting across banking partners, including minimum cash balances required in specific accounts.
  • Responsible for weekly cash flow funding and support medium term cash forecasting, incorporating expected payments, project-level requirements, liquidity needs, and corporate cash views.
  • Management of short term cash investments including term deposits and MMFs.
  • Support ongoing bank KYC requirements in conjunction with Company Secretariat and maintain disciplined records for bank access and authority arrangements.

Hedging

  • Manage day-to-day FX requirements in line with weekly cash flow funding
  • Support the GM Treasury in developing the Group’s hedging strategy.
  • Coordinate FX and derivative confirmations and settlements.
  • Support hedge accounting documentation, valuations, CVA/DVA measurement inputs, and effectiveness testing processes.

Bank Guarantees

  • Coordinate execution, issuance, amendment, tracking, and release of bank guarantees as required by the business.
  • Maintain a bank guarantee register and support accounting for guarantee fees, including upfront fees released to profit and loss over time.

Reporting, Controls & Compliance

  • Prepare monthly treasury and facility reporting, including cash balances, controlled account reconciliations, operating reporting, covenant model updates, and project-level treasury inputs.
  • Support reporting required for customer contracts, lender requirements, equity investor requirements, and SPV funding arrangements.
  • Prepare monthly counterparty credit reporting covering investments, mark-to-market positions, exposures, and treasury counterparty risk.
  • Assist with audit reporting on treasury control and process compliance, including bank platform access reviews and segregation of duties.

Intercompany & Treasury Systems

  • Support accounting and reporting for cross-entity bank transfers, cross-border balances, and ring-fenced entity balances.
  • Lead or support treasury management system implementation, including facility capture, hedging workflows, valuation and effectiveness testing setup, and treasury reporting.
  • Work with Finance Systems to implement automated bank statements into NetSuite and the treasury management system, and support straight-through processing for AP and treasury payments.
  • Identify opportunities to improve treasury processes, controls, documentation, automation, and reporting cadence as Firmus scales.**

###

Skills & Experience

Required Skills

  • 8-10+ years experience in treasury operations, corporate treasury, project finance operations, banking, or a related finance role.
  • Strong understanding of debt facility administration, cash management, payments, bank accounts, covenants, interest accruals, fees, and treasury reporting.
  • Working knowledge of FX, derivatives, confirmations, settlements, hedge accounting support, valuations, and treasury counterparty reporting.
  • Strong financial systems capability, with experience using ERP, banking platforms, treasury management systems, payment automation and AI tools.
  • High attention to detail, strong control mindset, and ability to manage deadlines across multiple workstreams.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with ability to coordinate effectively across Finance, Legal, CoSec, banks, advisors, and internal stakeholders.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience in a high-growth infrastructure, technology, energy, data centre, project finance, or listed-company environment.
  • Familiarity with lender reporting, covenant models, controlled accounts, liquidity requirements and intercompany funding.

Location & Reporting

  • Location: Sydney, Australia
  • Reports to: General Manager, Treasure

###

Employment Basis

Permanent full-time

Diversity

At Firmus, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are passionate about creating a more sustainable future through innovative engineering solutions.

Join us in our mission to revolutionise the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

Role Summary

Firmus Technologies is seeking a Senior Power Systems SCADA and Controls Engineer to support the SCADA, HMI, telemetry and control systems associated with Firmus’ MV, HV and EHV electrical infrastructure. This is a hands-on technical role for someone with strong power systems SCADA and controls capability who wants to apply those skills in a new and fast-growing infrastructure sector.

Firmus’ Model-to-Grid capability is our approach to operating large AI compute loads as controllable, grid-responsive electrical infrastructure. In practical terms, this means using SCADA, telemetry, signal interfaces, operating limits, runback schemes, ramp-rate controls and HMI visibility to manage how workload responds to grid, network and operational requirements.

This role sits on the power systems controller side of that capability. The successful candidate will help translate TNSP, AEMO and grid connection requirements into practical Firmus-side control schemes, while working with Firmus’ HPC and internal controls teams to integrate those schemes with advanced AI workload management and load control systems.

Prior AI or data centre experience is not essential. What matters is strong power systems SCADA, controls, telemetry and commissioning capability, and an interest in applying those skills to a new class of controllable infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build, configure and support the code, control logic, SCADA/HMI screens, telemetry and operator interfaces required to deliver Model-to-Grid power controller functions.
  • Develop and support interfaces for agreed network and protection schemes, including runback triggers, load-reduction commands and Firmus-side controls required to support special protection schemes.
  • Work with grid connections, HPC and internal controls teams to translate power network requirements into practical SCADA, HMI and control logic on Firmus’ side of the connection point.
  • Work with HPC and AI Platform teams to integrate Model-to-Grid control capability with Firmus’ AI compute platform, enabling advanced workload management, load control and grid-responsive operation.
  • Support configuration, testing and commissioning of SCADA, HMI, telemetry and controls for MV/HV/EHV infrastructure and related Firmus-side load control interfaces.
  • Configure and support gateways, RTUs and power system control platforms, directly or through consultants and OEMs as appropriate.
  • Develop practical SCADA/HMI deliverables, including operator screens, alarm structures, point maps, control sequences, operating limits and commissioning records.

Skills & Experience

  • Practical experience in power systems SCADA, HMI, automation, substation control systems or industrial power system controls.
  • Experience with MV, HV or EHV infrastructure, substations, utilities, grid connections,
  • Experience with Ignition SCADA is highly desirable.
  • Experience with SEL relays, SEL RTACs or similar SEL automation/control platforms is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with DNP3, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, IEC 61850 and industrial Ethernet.
  • Ability to read single line diagrams, protection/control schematics, network drawings, I/O lists, point schedules and functional descriptions.
  • Strong troubleshooting, commissioning support and documentation skills.
  • Interest in applying traditional power systems SCADA and controls experience to a new class of controllable AI infrastructure.

Location

Based in: Launceston, Tasmania

Firmus would be open to consider suitable candidates to be based in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, depending on experience and ability to support Firmus’ national project pipeline

Full-time

The successful candidate will combine strong technical accounting skills with a proactive approach to process improvement, helping to build a scalable and well-controlled finance function capable of supporting future growth.

While external reporting and audit support form part of the role, the primary focus is on financial operations, close management, balance sheet governance, management reporting and the delivery of accurate financial outcomes that enable effective decision-making across the business.

Month-End Close & Financial Accounting

  • Lead the end-to-end month-end and year-end close process, ensuring accurate, timely and complete financial reporting across the Group.

Financial Control, CAPEX & Balance Sheet Governance

Skills & Experience

job.title: Principal Solutions Architect, AI Data Infrastructure
job.description:
Firmus Technology

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

Role Summary

We are seeking a Principal Solution Architect, AI Data Infrastructure to serve as Firmus’s subject-matter expert on everywhere data lives and moves across the AI fabric—storage, memory, and the caching layers that keep GPUs fully utilised. You will own the architecture, evaluation, and optimisation of the systems that feed our AI Factory and Firmus AI Cloud, from high-performance parallel and software-defined storage, through NVMe and next-generation memory fabrics, to the KV-cache and data-movement paths that determine real training and inference performance. In a business built on making every watt count, your job is to make every byte count with it.

You will operate as the trusted technical authority across both internal engineering teams and external customers – translating complex data-path decisions into measurable performance, capacity, and TCO outcomes. Whether validating a customer’s workload requirements or shaping our own platform roadmap, you’ll be the person who understands the principles deeply enough that specific vendors and brands are secondary to the architecture.

Key Responsibilities

You’ll own the reference architecture for the AI data path end to end—parallel and software-defined storage, NVMe and NVMe-oF, object and file systems, memory disaggregation and pooling, and the KV-cache and data-movement strategies that eliminate bottlenecks between storage, memory, and GPUs. You’ll evaluate, benchmark, and select technologies against real AI workloads, turning results into clear decisions on performance, capacity, power efficiency, and total cost of ownership.

Depending on the engagement, you’ll work externally as the trusted advisor to customers, sizing solutions, validating requirements, and resolving performance issues in production – or internally, shaping the platform roadmap and integrating storage and memory into our Kubernetes-based and bare-metal environments alongside compute and networking teams. Either way, you’ll bring the low-latency fabric expertise (RDMA, RoCEv2, InfiniBand) to connect it all, and establish the operational best practices for data protection, resilience, and lifecycle management that a large-scale cloud demands.

Skills & Experience

You’ll bring deep, vendor-agnostic expertise across the AI data path, with hands-on experience of one or more leading high-performance storage and memory platforms—systems in the class of WEKA, VAST Data, DDN, or Dell (PowerScale/PowerFlex)—understanding the underlying principles well enough that the specific brand is secondary. You’re fluent in NVMe and NVMe-oF, parallel and software-defined storage, object and file systems, and the low-latency network fabrics (RDMA, RoCEv2, InfiniBand) that link data to GPUs, and you track next-generation memory directions such as CXL, memory disaggregation, and KV-cache optimisation for LLM workloads.

Just as important is benchmarking discipline – you can design and run workload-driven evaluations across bare-metal, virtualised, and containerised environments and translate the numbers into architecture and business cases. You’ve done this at scale, integrating storage and memory into GPU clusters (DGX/HGX and similar) and reasoning about the CAPEX, server-count, and power trade-offs that come with it. Typically this comes with 10+ years in storage, memory, HPC, or AI infrastructure roles.

Communication rounds it out. You can advise a C-level customer, author a clear reference architecture or whitepaper, and mentor engineers with equal ease, and you’re comfortable in high-ambiguity environments where the right architecture has to be created rather than copied.

Key Competencies

You bring deep command of the full AI data path – storage, memory, and cache – and back it with rigorous, workload-driven benchmarking. You think in systems, reasoning fluently across compute, network, and data, and you stay pragmatic and vendor-agnostic, optimising for outcomes rather than badges. You operate as a single-threaded owner, driving to the outcome, and you communicate with equal ease across engineering teams and executive audiences.

Location & Reporting

  • Singapore
  • Reporting to the Director of Solution Architecture & Delivery

Employment Basis

Full-time

Diversity

At Firmus, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are passionate about creating a more sustainable future through innovative engineering solutions.

Join us in our mission to revolutionize the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

The ideal candidate will play a crucial role in leading the development of our network designs and supporting the network deployment for AI infrastructure projects. This role offers an exciting opportunity to work at the forefront of AI networking technology and contribute to the growth of AI infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Design, Implement and Maintain Network Infrastructure

  • Architect, deploy, support the corporate LAN, WAN, WLAN, and VPN infrastructure.
  • Ensure high availability, performance and security of on-premise and cloud-connected network services.
  • Setup, configure and maintain secure site-tp-site VPNs, MPLS links, or private interconnects between data centres, customer site, cloud environments and partner networks.

Network as Code and Automation

  • Develop and maintain automated network configurations using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools (eg: Ansible, Netbox, Python scripts)
  • Implement CI/CD pipelines for network changes to improve speed, consistency, and auditability
  • Automate routine tasks such as provisioning, backups and compliance checks.

Network Security and Policy Enforcement

  • Implement and manage firewall and security devices. Apply firewall rules, VLAN segmentation, ACLs and zero-trust principles to safeguard internal and external communications.
  • Collaborate with SMC Security and Risk team to enforce policies and respond to security incidents.

Operation Support

  • Respond and resolve escalate network issues, outages and performance degradations across the SMC Corporate and Compute network infrastructure.
  • Analyze logs, run diagnostics and coordinate with vendors, carriers as needed.
  • Work with internal observability team to setup and maintain monitoring tools to proactively identify bottlenecks, errors and abnormal behaviours.
  • Analyze trends for bandwidth, hardware utilization, and growth to inform scaling and make recommendation to procurement decisions.
  • Design and rest redundant paths, failover mechanisms and DR playbooks to ensure uninterrupted connectivity during outages or maintenance.
  • Participate in operation standby roster and on-call for time to time.

Project Management and Stakeholder Management

  • Support the deployment team in their project management and resource allocation for the network portion of AI cluster installations.
  • Collaborate and work closely with Global Operation Centre, Software Defined Infrastructure team, Data Centre Infrastructure team and Solution Architects to support deployments and to maintain SLAs.

Technology Expertise

  • Maintain and expand expertise in physical network hardware and advanced networking technologies, including (i) NVIDIA InfiniBand; (ii) Spectrum Ethernet Platform, and (iii) RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE).
  • Familiar with open source network operating systems such as Cumulus Linux and Sonic
  • Maintain and expand expertise in NetDevOps practices to maintain software defined network infrastructure
  • Provide technical support and troubleshooting for advanced networking technologies, escalating to vendors as needed.
  • Mentor junior network engineers, assisting with their technical development.

Stakeholder Management

  • Work closely with both Firmus Engineering and Commissioning teams to align network infrastructure with customers’ requirements.

  • Maintain and build strong relationships with key technology partners and vendors and proactively manage and coordinate partner engagement on site.

Skills & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in network engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.

  • Strong project management skills and experienced in complex technical projects.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.
  • Willingness to undertake international and/or domestic travel for on-site deployments and commissioning.
  • Solid understanding of advanced networking technologies, particularly those related to AI would be highly advantageous.
  • Hands-on experience with NVIDIA InfiniBand, Spectrum Ethernet Platform, and/or RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) preferred.

Key Competencies

  • Enterprise & AI network delivery (LAN, WAN, WLAN, VPN)
  • Secure connectivity (site-to-site VPN, MPLS, private interconnects)
  • Network automation & NetDevOps (IaC, Ansible, Python, CI/CD)
  • Network security (firewalls, VLANs, ACLs, zero-trust)
  • Operations, monitoring & incident response
  • AI networking tech (InfiniBand, Spectrum, RoCE)

Full-time

Diversity

Join us in our mission to revolutionize the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

job.title: Mechanical Project Engineer
job.description:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the solution to AI’s energy challenge, founded in Australia in 2019 by a visionary team of entrepreneurs. Our mission is to create the most energy-efficient AI infrastructure, combining cutting edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

Through ground-breaking research and development, we invented a verticalized AI Factory - a new class of digital infrastructure that replaces traditional data centres. Built on new approaches to liquid cooling, energy management, water use and modular construction methodology, the Firmus AI Factory delivers low-cost AI tokens across Asia-Pacific.

Firmus AI Cloud

We provide customers access to energy savings via our large-scale GPU cloud, Firmus AI Cloud. Rated Silver in The GPU Cloud ClusterMAX™ Rating System, our cloud empowers developers, enterprise, education and government users to train AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing list of services and applications, we are committed to building a cloud experience for our customers that is market-leading, proprietary and built to scale.

Why you’ll love working here

  • A fast-paced and dynamic environment working with next-gen technology. You’ll be operating at the intersection of sustainability and artificial intelligence – helping to transform an industry.
  • Working with and access to colleagues who are true innovators and leaders in their field.
  • As an emerging company, we work as a close-knit team. Work with the founders, grow a strong network, and witness the impact you make first-hand as we democratise AI tools for everyone – more sustainably, and more affordably.
  • We believe that people from diverse backgrounds come together to do their best work, be their authentic selves, and build great things. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

About the Role

Firmus Technologies is seeking a Mechanical Project Engineer with project engineering experience in the mechanical design, delivery and commissioning to join our Engineering and Technology team. The successful candidate will be involved from late-stage design, through site construction, commissioning and handover into operations of Firmus’ state-of-the-art sustainable AI Factory developments.

You will act as the owner’s engineer onsite, ensuring the mechanical aspects of our AI Factory builds are delivered safely, on time, to budget and in accordance with our design, standards and project objectives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design management for detailed mechanical designs delivered by contractors, ensuring alignment with Firmus standards and project requirements.
  • Carry out engineering design and calculations to provide technical guidance and direction to contractors.
  • Review contractor mechanical drawings, documentation and equipment selections against contractual obligations, industry standards, safety compliance, and best practice.
  • Assist with the management of project documentation, including RFIs, variation requests, change control records, and site instructions for mechanical works.
  • Attending site and progress meetings to assist as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) in the mechanical subject area
  • Conduct regular site inspections to verify that the installations are in line with approved drawings, specifications and quality requirements.
  • Track progress against milestones for mechanical scope, identify deviations, and recommend recovery or mitigation actions.
  • Prepares ITPs and checklists that accurately tests equipment and plant to confirm they meets the contractual and performance requirements.
  • Review ITPs and test documentation prepared by contractors for mechanical scopes of work, providing feedback and approvals where appropriate.
  • Participate in QA inspections (incl. factory acceptance tests), commissioning of mechanical systems and Integrated Systems Testing to ensure plant, equipment and systems meet contract requirements and are tuned for optimum performance.
  • Provide on‑the‑ground oversight of mechanical contractor commissioning activities, ensuring tests are executed as per approved procedures, issues are captured and resolved, and systems are validated prior to handover.
  • Contribute to the creation of Operation and Maintenance manuals that shall include all maintenance requirements of systems and equipment.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering.
  • 3+ years of project engineer experience in mechanical contracting, design or construction. Experience in data centre or other critical environment projects will be highly regarded.
  • Strong understanding of mechanical design principles, methodologies, and relevant Australian standards, with the ability to interpret drawings and technical documentation.
  • Demonstrated analytical problem-solving skills with the ability to work with ambiguous problems and develop effective and innovative technical solutions.
  • Detail-oriented approach to work to ensure accuracy in design and testing and strong clear documentation.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate ideas and convey technical information to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience of working in a cross-functional multi-cultural teams and collaborating effectively with contractors, vendors and internal stakeholders.
  • Excellent organisation and time‑management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced project environment.
  • Strong willingness to learn and proactively contribute to team and organisational goals.
  • Flexibility to adapt to evolving project requirements and priorities, with an eagerness to take on new responsibilities and learn on the job.
  • Proficiency in using computer-aided design (CAD) software to draft mechanical schematics is also desirable

LOCATION

Launceston, TAS – Australia;

EMPLOYMENT BASIS

Full-Time

job.title: Head of Electrical Engineering, AI Factory Development
job.description:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

Roles & Responsibilities

As Head of Electrical Engineering, AI Factory Development at Firmus, you will lead the electrical engineering discipline across every site where Firmus is building and scaling an AI Factory. This is a principal-engineer-equivalent management role within the Build group, accountable for the consistent, high-quality implementation of Firmus's reference electrical design across our global site portfolio.

The role sits within AI Factory Development (Build) and reports to the Head/Director of AI Factory Engineering. You will lead a distributed team of site-based electrical engineers across Indonesia, Australia, and any future geography where Firmus is active. Your remit is delivery, governance, and technical assurance of the electrical design in construction, commissioning, and handover — not ownership of the reference design itself, though you will be a primary and continuous input into the reference design's evolution.

This is a central leadership role. You are the single accountable owner for electrical engineering execution across the Firmus AI Factory estate, the escalation point for electrical technical issues in the field, and the guardian of design intent from tender through energisation. You will work in tight partnership with the reference design owners, the Mechanical and Thermal, Controls, and Physical Networking Heads, and with Construction, Commissioning, and Operations to ensure every site is electrically built, tested, and handed over to standard.

What you will do

As Head of Electrical Engineering, AI Factory Development, you will own the electrical engineering function within the AI Factory Development group. You will define how the reference electrical design is interpreted, adapted for local codes and site conditions, procured, constructed, and commissioned across every Firmus site. You will set the technical bar for MV/LV distribution, UPS and standby generation, protection and coordination, earthing and bonding, power quality, and the electrical interfaces to liquid-cooled AI compute halls.

You will act as the engineering authority for electrical execution across the AI Factory portfolio — accountable for design governance in the field, deviation management, factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning readiness, and safe, reliable energisation. You will operate the change-control and design-review disciplines that keep every site aligned to the Firmus reference design, and you will be the escalation point when local realities require considered deviation or when the reference design itself needs to evolve.

You will not own the development of the reference electrical design, but you will be one of its most important customers and contributors. You will feed operational learnings, site constraints, vendor performance data, and commissioning findings back into the reference design owners, and you will co-develop the electrical standards, templates, and Basis of Design updates that keep Firmus's design ahead of the industry.

You will build, lead, and scale a geographically distributed electrical engineering team – site-based engineers embedded in Indonesia, Australia, and any additional geography where Firmus operates. You will set the operating rhythm across time zones, establish consistent engineering practice and quality standards across sites, develop the next generation of senior electrical engineers within Firmus, and represent electrical engineering in cross-functional Build, Commissioning, and Operations forums.

Skills & Experiences

You are, first and foremost, an accomplished electrical engineer for mission-critical, high-density digital infrastructure. You bring deep expertise in medium- and low-voltage distribution, UPS systems, standby and prime-power generation, static and rotary switching, protection and relay coordination, arc-flash and safety-in-design, earthing and bonding, and the specific electrical demands of dense GPU compute halls and liquid-cooled AI infrastructure. You understand power system modelling — load flow, short-circuit, motor starting, transient stability — and you have used it to make consequential design and operational decisions.

Across the delivery lifecycle, you are equally at home leading tender design reviews, consultant and contractor governance, factory acceptance testing, integrated systems testing, level-1 through level-5 commissioning, and handover to operations. You have authored or materially shaped Basis of Design documents, engineering templates, global minimum standards, and change-control processes at a hyperscale operator or equivalent. You are comfortable engaging utilities, regulators, and major equipment vendors, and you know how to drive value engineering, DfMA, and sustainability outcomes without compromising reliability.

Above all, you have the temperament of a senior technical leader operating across geographies: strong systems thinking, calm judgement under construction and commissioning pressure, the confidence to challenge design and vendor assumptions constructively, and the communication skill to carry a room of site engineers, a customer technical review, and an executive readout with equal clarity. You bring commercial awareness, comfort operating across cultures and time zones, and a genuine passion for building AI infrastructure that works reliably from day one.

**

The ideal candidate will bring a strong technical foundation in electrical power engineering, ideally with a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering (power systems preferred) recognised in at least one of Firmus's operating jurisdictions, together with more than 12 years of progressive experience across hyperscale or mission-critical data centre developments, industrial power systems, or comparable high-availability infrastructure. They will have deep, hands-on expertise as an electrical subject-matter expert and design manager on multi-site programmes, and a proven track record leading design governance, quality assurance, and commissioning readiness across a portfolio of concurrent projects.

This experience should include leading distributed, site-based engineering teams across multiple countries, managing external consultants and EPC contractors to global standards, and working effectively across the build-to-run interface with Construction, Commissioning, and Operations. Experience authoring or contributing materially to global electrical Basis of Design, minimum standards, or reference architecture at a hyperscale, cloud, or specialist AI infrastructure operator is a strong differentiator, as is experience delivering into APAC markets — particularly Indonesia and Australia — under diverse regulatory, grid, and utility conditions.

Location & Reporting

  • Australia, or Singapore (with regular travel across the AI Factory portfolio)
  • Reporting to the Head/Director of AI Factory Engineering

Through ground-breaking research and development, we invented a verticalized AI Factory - a new class of digital infrastructure that replaces traditional data centres. Built on new approaches to liquid cooling, energy management, water use and modular construction methodology, the Firmus AI Factory delivers low-cost AI tokens across Asia-Pacific.

Firmus AI Cloud

We provide customers access to energy savings via our large-scale GPU cloud, Firmus AI Cloud. Rated Silver in The GPU Cloud ClusterMAX™ Rating System, our cloud empowers developers, enterprise, education and government users to train AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing list of services and applications, we are committed to building a cloud experience for our customers that is market-leading, proprietary and built to scale.

Why you’ll love working here

  • A fast-paced and dynamic environment working with next-gen technology. You’ll be operating at the intersection of sustainability and artificial intelligence – helping to transform an industry.
  • Working with and access to colleagues who are true innovators and leaders in their field.
  • As an emerging company, we work as a close-knit team. Work with the founders, grow a strong network, and witness the impact you make first-hand as we democratise AI tools for everyone – more sustainably, and more affordably.
  • We believe that people from diverse backgrounds come together to do their best work, be their authentic selves, and build great things. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

ROLE SUMMARY

The Field Service Technician is a hands-on team player who will play a crucial role in ensuring the efficient deployment, operation, maintenance, and repair of our HyperCube systems. The ideal candidate will be responsible for keeping our site operations running smoothly through providing high-quality technical support, troubleshooting issues, and maintaining a strong customer relationship while adhering to safety and quality standards. This role requires on-site support and a willingness to tackle various tasks, including maintenance, repair, and manual labour.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Equipment Maintenance & Repair: Inspect, maintain, install, and repair mechanical, electrical, fibre network ,and ancillary systems to ensure reliable operation.
  • Troubleshooting & Fault Resolution: Diagnose and resolve technical issues efficiently, applying practical solutions and escalating when necessary.
  • Deployment & Commissioning Support:

Assist with installations of equipment, modifications, and setup under the direction of the site manager.

  • Support HyperCube fluid handling (fill/drain) and load bank installation/removal during commissioning.
  • Assist with network cabling and integration.
  • Support site teams during commissioning, testing, and equipment setup.
  • Operations & Site Management: Perform basic fault-finding, reset circuits/pumps, remove and repair faulty equipment, maintain site cleanliness, and comply with OHS requirements.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Provide timely updates and technical support to project and operations teams, ensuring smooth collaboration.
  • Documentation & Reporting: Keep accurate service records, equipment logs, and submit required documentation promptly.
  • Safety & Compliance: Adhere to safety protocols, maintain PPE, first aid kits, and eyewash stations.
  • Training & Development: Stay current on equipment, processes, and industry standards through ongoing learning.
  • Inventory & Quality Control: Maintain tools, spare parts, and equipment inventory; conduct quality checks post-maintenance or repair.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Familiarity with fibre hygiene and testing fibre networks.
  • Familiarity with data centre apparatus is a plus.
  • Diploma or equivalent, technical certification, trade qualification.
  • At least 3 years of relevant experience in a similar role, including hands-on experience with equipment maintenance and repair.
  • Good problem-solving and communication skills. Proven to be able to work effectively under direction.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, as this position is part of a 24/7 operating roster.
  • Must hold an unrestricted driver’s license.
  • Electrical license (for electrical staff only).

Location

This role is based on-site in Brooklyn, Melbourne, Australia.

Employment Basis

Permanent full-time

Diversity

At Firmus, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are passionate about creating a more sustainable future through innovative engineering solutions.

Join us in our mission to revolutionise the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

job.title: Energy Manager
job.description:
Goodman owns and manages one of Australia's largest commercial rooftop solar portfolios, with more than 400 solar installations across a substantial national property portfolio. As our renewable energy platform continues to mature, we're looking for an Energy Manager to help drive the operational performance, compliance and future optimisation of these assets.

This role is ideal for someone wanting to move from a contractor, consultancy, retailer or service provider environment into an owner-side position where they can influence strategy while managing a large and diverse energy portfolio.

About the Role

Reporting to the Head of Energy, you will be responsible for the ongoing operation and performance of Goodman Australia's energy assets, including solar PV, battery energy storage systems, EV charging infrastructure and utility metering.

While new energy projects remain part of the role, the primary focus is operational excellence. You'll take ownership of the day-to-day management of the portfolio, working with service providers, retailers, property teams and customers to ensure assets perform safely, efficiently and compliantly.

You'll become the business's energy subject matter expert, helping internal stakeholders understand performance data, identify opportunities and make informed commercial decisions.

  • Oversee maintenance providers, service agreements and asset performance.
  • Support energy procurement activities and retailer engagement.
  • Manage solar registrations and renewable energy certificate requirements.
  • Analyse energy and environmental data to identify trends, risks and opportunities.
  • Deliver reporting, dashboards and insights that support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Provide advice to Property and Development teams on customer energy opportunities.
  • Support sustainability reporting, assurance processes and compliance obligations.
  • Investigate operational incidents, performance issues and emerging risks.
  • Contribute to future initiatives including battery storage, customer energy solutions and microgrid opportunities.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience managing operational renewable energy or utility assets across multiple sites.
  • Strong understanding of solar PV systems and energy management principles.
  • Experience working with energy retailers, metering providers and utility data.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyse complex datasets and translate findings into practical recommendations.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and commercial acumen.
  • Knowledge of renewable energy, compliance and reporting frameworks.
  • A degree in Engineering, Environmental Science or a related discipline.

Why Join Goodman?

This is a rare opportunity to join the owner of one of Australia's largest commercial rooftop solar portfolios and help shape the next phase of our energy journey.

You'll gain exposure to a diverse asset base, work closely with customers and internal stakeholders, and help influence how energy, sustainability and technology continue to evolve across the business.

Beyond managing today's assets, you'll help explore future opportunities in battery storage, customer energy solutions, EV infrastructure and microgrid development.

job.title: Manager/Senior Manager, Commercial Project Management – New Subsea Cable Projects
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

We are seeking an experienced Commercial Project Manager to own the commercial development and delivery of new subsea cable projects — from investment origination and underwriting, through financing, entity structuring and contract award, to installation, commercialization and handover to operations.

You will act as the commercial owner of assigned projects, working across engineering, fund management, corporate finance, legal and tax to ensure each project is investable, bankable, properly structured, and delivered on time and on budget. This is a high-visibility role for someone equally comfortable building an underwriting model, negotiating a facility agreement, and managing a supply-and-installation contract.

Key Areas of Ownership 1: Investment underwriting

  • Building the investment underwriting model (with the Investment team) for new subsea cable projects, working closely with colleagues from Keppel's Fund Management & Investment (FM&I) platform who are responsible for raising external investments
  • Develop and maintain the full project financial model: capex and opex build-up, capacity sales assumptions (IRUs, leases, spectrum), revenue phasing, returns analysis (IRR, MOIC, payback) and sensitivity/scenario testing.
  • Support investment committee papers and approvals, ensuring underwriting assumptions are robust, defensible and aligned with fund co-investor requirements.
  • Track actual project performance against underwriting through the project life cycle and report variances with mitigation plans.
  • Build and own monthly, quarterly exec level Project reporting across all commercial parameters with project dashboard tracking on key risks, mitigations and delivery plans

2: Project financing

  • Work with Keppel's corporate finance team to engage with various lenders (commercial banks, ECAs and institutional lenders) and support the structuring and execution of project debt.
  • Lead the workstream to put in place the Facility Agreement (FA), coordinating lender due diligence, term sheet negotiation, conditions precedent and financial close.
  • Ensure all obligations under the FA are met throughout the project life cycle — including covenant compliance, reporting obligations, drawdown conditions, insurance requirements and lender consents for variations.
  • Act as the day-to-day interface with facility agents, lenders' technical advisers and insurers post-close.

3: Entity formation and tax structuring

  • Work with legal, finance and tax colleagues to ensure entity formation and holding/tax structures for each project are sound, efficient and compliant across all relevant jurisdictions.
  • Coordinate the establishment of project SPVs, joint venture vehicles and consortium structures, including shareholder agreements and joint build arrangements.
  • Ensure licensing and regulatory prerequisites tied to the corporate structure (e.g. landing licenses, FBO/telecoms licenses, cable landing approvals) are identified and secured in the right entities at the right time.

4: Commercial delivery

  • Own the overall System Budget along with Keppel share and mange Keppel Total Investment Cost Budgets, forecasts, cash flow and margin protection; track committed vs. actual spend and report variances.
  • Own the creation and execution of all key commercial agreements (PDMA, SSHA, OMA, FA) to enable the project.
  • Assist the preparation and modeling of supply and installation contracts (cable manufacture, marine installation, survey, burial and landing station works, terrestrial fiber, etc).
  • Assist in managing variations, claims and disputes; protect Keppel's contractual position and drive timely resolution.
  • Assist in negotiating and modeling of crossing and proximity agreements with other seabed users, and support permitting and consenting workstreams where commercial terms intersect with regulatory obligations.
  • Assist in negotiating and modeling of all key customer and partner contract

5: Commercialization and stakeholders

  • Support with capacity commercialization strategy and analysis — IRU sales, leases and anchor customer agreements with hyperscalers and carriers — in coordination with the Business Development Team.
  • Act as the primary commercial interface with consortium partners, landing parties, fund co-investors and joint build partners.
  • Maintain the project risk register from a commercial perspective; quantify exposure and lead mitigation.
  • Prepare monthly and quarterly board and management reporting on project commercial status, risks and opportunities.

Join our vibrant and inclusive workforce to shape a better future for all!

#LI-AM1

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Required Skills

  • 5+ years' commercial project management, investment or project finance experience, with meaningful exposure to subsea cables, telecoms infrastructure, or large-scale offshore/energy projects.
  • Strong financial modelling and underwriting capability on capital projects, ideally including investor/fund reporting.
  • Direct experience with project financing: lender engagement, facility agreements, financial close and ongoing covenant/obligation management.
  • Working knowledge of cross-border entity structuring, SPVs and joint venture arrangements, and the ability to work effectively with legal and tax advisers.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills at senior and board level.
  • Willingness to travel internationally, including to manufacturing facilities, vessels and landing sites.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with submarine telecoms systems (wet plant, SLTE, landing stations) and capacity commercialization (IRUs, spectrum sales).
  • Familiarity with consortium/joint build structures, regulatory agreements, ICPC recommendations and cable landing licensing regimes (e.g. IMDA FBO licences, US FCC landing licences).
  • Experience with ECA-backed financing or private fund co-investment structures.
  • Degree in finance, engineering, business or law; CFA, MBA or contract management qualification a plus.

BUSINESS SEGMENT

Connectivity

PLATFORM

Operating Division
